job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

response.passage: Rohan and his sister Meera were looking at a globe in their living room in Delhi. Meera traced a horizontal circle and asked if it was a painted line on the ground. Rohan laughed and explained that these are imaginary lines called latitudes used for location. He pointed to the vertical lines, the longitudes, which meet at the poles, unlike the parallel latitudes. Meera then asked why the area near the Equator feels so hot. Rohan explained that the Earth is a sphere, and the Sun's rays fall directly on the Torrid Zone, concentrating heat in a small area, not because of the distance to the Sun. They then looked at their watches. Rohan noted that when it is noon in Delhi, it is not noon in London. He explained that as the Earth rotates from west to east, places east of the Prime Meridian see the sunrise earlier. To keep things simple, India follows the 82.5°E longitude as its standard time, which is different from the Prime Meridian. Meera finally understood that time depends on the Earth's rotation, and these lines help us navigate our vast world without needing any physical markings on the planet's surface.
response.summary: The passage explains that latitudes and longitudes are imaginary lines used for navigation and timekeeping. It clarifies that the Earth's heat zones depend on the angle of sunlight, and time varies across the globe due to the Earth's rotation.
